entries.title: Isaiah 42:1
segments: My servant; the Messiah.

The reference to Cyrus in the preceding chapter naturally prepared the way for the mention of one greater than Cyrus. 
 
vv 1-4. 
 
The kingdom of Christ "cometh not with observation," but by the gentle and quiet influences of his word and Spirit operating within the soul. Great outward changes and revolutions accompany its progress in the world, but amid all these it remains "like leaven which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened."

entries.title: Isaiah 42:2
segments: Lift up; his voice; he shall be quiet and unassuming.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:5
segments:
He that created--spirit to them that walk therein; the divine power set forth in this verse is a pledge that the promise contained in the following verse shall be fulfilled. 
 
vv 5-8. 
 
God's glory is pledged to establish Christ's kingdom over all the earth, and to give deliverance and salvation to every sinner who commits his soul to His hands.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:7
segments: To open the blind eyes--out of the prison-house; he is the Redeemer from spiritual blindness and bondage.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:8
segments: My glory will I not give to another--to graven images; by allowing the cause of idolatry to triumph.  Thus God pledges his own glory for the success of the Messiah and his kingdom.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:9
segments: The former things; the things formerly predicted.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:10
segments:
A new song; for the new things declared. 
 
vv 10-16. 
 
The same mighty movements of God's providence and Spirit which bring salvation and rejoicing to his church, carry desolation and destruction into the hosts of her enemies.  While they weep and wail over the fall of Satan's kingdom, she shouts, "Alleluia," as its smoke rises up for ever and ever.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:17
segments:
vv 17-25. 
 
The hope of God's people is his zeal for the glory of his own name.  He will not give them over to final corruption and ruin, but will, from time to time, purify them by severe judgments, and thus prepare the way for the extension of Christ's kingdom over all the earth.

entries.title: Isaiah 42:19
segments: My servant; Israel, the covenant people of God.  "The servant of the Lord" signifies, in its widest sense, any minister of his will, though he be ignorant of God as Nebuchadnezzar,
. Compare

.  In a more special sense it is applied, particularly in this part of Isaiah, 
 
(1) to God's visible covenant people, "Israel after the flesh," as in this verse,

, and often elsewhere; 
 
(2) to the body of true believers, "the Israel of God," contained within the outward Israel,

, etc.; 
 
(3) to Christ the Head of the church, as in

, and elsewhere. 
 
And as Christ and his true church are one body--

--it is often both difficult and unnecessary to determine whether the words "my servant" apply to Christ alone, or to Christ's body as quickened and sanctified by its union with him. 
 
  My messanger; Israel, whom God appointed to make the Gentiles see and hear his truth, has himself become blind and deaf. 
 
  Perfect; in respect to his privileges and outward relations to God. Compare

entries.title: Isaiah 42:21
segments:
Is well pleased; it is his good pleasure to do what is expressed in the last clause of the verse. 
 
  For his righteousness' sake; his covenant people having forfeited all claim to his favor by their sins, he will do this for the glory of his own name and character. 
 
  Will magnify the law; will put honor upon it by all his dealings with his people, and, in a most emphatic sense, by the mission and propitiatory death of his Son.
